assertions.text: The expected output column contains bonus percentages (e.g. 15%, 12%, 0%) — not bonus amounts. The method returns a percentage, and the table should reflect that.

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body: Employee employee = new Employee(...); assertEquals(...); no conditional statements

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case (e.g. 'bonusByLevelAndDepartment' → 'Bonus By Level And Department'). Not a generic name like 'test1' or 'testMethod'.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Bonus percentage by level and department") and method name calculatesBonusPercentage

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as how bonus rates are applied (e.g. as percentage of base salary), or open questions. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show. It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context.
assertions.evidence: @Description annotation is absent; table conveys scenario conditions and expected percentages sufficiently

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior in Sales', 'Contractor regardless of department') — not outcomes ('Gets 15%', 'No bonus').
assertions.evidence: Scenarios: 'Senior in sales', 'Senior in engineering', 'Junior in sales', 'Junior in engineering', 'Contractor regardless of dept' (all condition-based)

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Level', 'Department', 'Bonus %') — not implementation terms like 'employeeLevel', 'deptCode', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: Column header 'Bonus?' uses question mark format, unclear if value or yes/no question; assertion example 'Bonus %' clearly indicates percentage type
